We need retrosynthesis route for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH2 para? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amines? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the amide nitrogen attaches to a phenyl that has an NH at position 1 and another N at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino group at both ends? That's a diamino benzene (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide attaches to a phenyl with an NH at the other end.

Thus target is fairly complex. Need 3 steps max, leaves commercially available, total price < $9999.

We need to propose a retrosynthesis using templates. Approach: disconnection at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also disconnection at amide formation (acid chloride or activated acid + amine). Also disconnection at the C=C double bond (maybe Wittig or Heck). Simpler: we can think of building the central phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). Could be assembled via:

Step 1: Couple p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, TsCl) with an aniline (the phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2) has the sulfonamide attached to the tolyl ring via N. So we need the sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with the amine (the phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2) has the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group and also attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the central phenyl (c2ccc...). So we need to form sulfonamide between p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and an aniline (the phenyl ring with the rest). So step: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2) (the aniline). That yields the sulfonamide.

Thus we need to synthesize the aniline precursor: 4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). This can be formed via amide coupling between 4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-COOH (or acid chloride) and p-phenylenediamine (or aniline with NH2). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl with NH2 at para? The SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N indicates amide nitrogen attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent (maybe at para). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl at position 1, and that phenyl also has an NH2 at position? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with two amino groups at positions 1 and 6? Actually it's a benzene with N at position 1 (attached to carbonyl) and N at position 6 (free). So it's 1,2-diaminobenzene? Wait: "c3ccccc3" is benzene; preceding "N" attaches to first carbon; trailing "N" attaches to last carbon (position 1). So it's an aniline where the amide nitrogen is attached to the benzene, and there is another NH2 at the opposite carbon (para). So it's p-phenylenediamine where one amine is acylated.

Thus we can get p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and acylate one amine with the acid (4-aminophenyl-CH=CH-COOH) via selective acylation (maybe using protecting groups). But we have only 3 steps total, so we need simple route.

Alternative: Build the unsaturated amide via Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with acrylamide? Or via Knoevenagel condensation? Simpler: Use a known building block: trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or trans-3-phenylacryloyl chloride) reacting with p-phenylenediamine to give the amide (but that would give phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2) where the phenyl is phenyl of cinnamoyl (phenyl). That's exactly our unsaturated amide part: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). So we need trans-cinnamoyl chloride (commercial) and p-phenylenediamine (commercial). Reaction yields trans-cinnamoyl p-phenylenediamide (monoacylated). That gives the unsaturated amide with free NH2 on the other position.

Now we need to attach the sulfonyl phenyl (p-tolyl sulfonyl) to the free NH2 of that product (the aniline). So step 2: sulfonylation with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) to give final product.

Thus total steps: 2 steps (amide formation, sulfonylation). Both reagents are commercially available: trans-cinnamoyl chloride, p-phenylenediamine, p-toluenesulfonyl chloride. All likely cheap (<$100 each). So total price well under $9999.

Now we need to produce JSON route: root molecule target, children reaction step 2 (final step) with template id for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Need template ID. We need to search for template that forms sulfonamide. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] maybe.
